messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Elevated 5xx error rate from AZ3 egress to eu-west-1 observed (server: edge-proxy-az3) — possible network-layer drops. Alert threshold 5% sustained over 2m.
Sam: acked — oncall. looking now. any customer-facing impact?
SupportOps: seeing multiple customer reports of failed embedding calls and stalled streaming responses around 09:12 UTC. Tickets 7892, 7893.
Anya: I'm on network. pulling BGP/xflow. initial glance shows a spike in retransmits for paths via peer-asn 64521 and a lot of ICMP unreachable (frag needed).
Priya: timeline note: we rolled a router firmware update in az3 late last night but no obvious correlation from SRE alerts.
Sam: can you post relevant tcpdump/pkt logs? are these IPv4 or IPv6?
Anya: mostly v6. interestingly client connections are dual-stack but are preferring v6 (ADDR_PREFER = true). packets > 1500 are being dropped on egress to peer-asn. looks like jumbo-negotiation mismatch — PMTUD probes (ICMPv6 PTB) are being rate-limited by an upstream firewall, so hosts never discover the smaller MTU.
Priya: that matches some of the support traces: SYNs succeed, then we see large data segments get blackholed after exchange.
Sam: severity -> P1. notify customers? set status page?
SupportOps: starting incident status update draft. will post once we have mitigation.
Anya: mitigation idea 1 — temporarily clamp MSS on our edge egress for affected prefix to 1220. that's quick and low risk.
Mike: second idea — change routing policy to prefer IPv4 exit for the affected peer-ASN to avoid the broken v6 path. can be rolled back quickly.
Sam: do MSS clamp first (lower blast radius) while Mike prepares the routing fallback. Anya take the clamp. Priya coordinate with infra-bot for config push.
Anya: applying iptables mss clamping on edge-proxy-az3 now. command:```sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -o eth0 -m tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu```Applying to the egress chain for prefix 2001:db8:az3::/48.```
infra-bot: config-push started: pushing mangle rule to 6 hosts in az3-edge pool.
Anya: rule applied on 4/6 hosts; seeing immediate drop in retransmits on those. sampling logs:```
[09:15:23] edge-proxy-az3-2: TCP id=0x7f3 SRC=2001:db8:client->2001:db8:service LEN=1200 flags=S
[09:15:24] edge-proxy-az3-2: TCP id=0x7f3 SRC=2001:db8:client->2001:db8:service LEN=1200 flags=S (clamped -> 1220)
[09:15:30] edge-proxy-az3-2: retransmit count reduced
```
SupportOps: customers 7892/7893 reporting improvement :thumbsup:. status page draft ready.
Sam: good. Mike — prep route fallback in case we need it. include a canary to 10% of traffic.
Mike: will do. BGP change ready: prepend local to minimize preference for v6 exit and add community no-export to the affected prefix for az3-egress to force IPv4 path from partners. will push to routers in 2 mins if needed.
Anya: rolling the clamp to remaining 2 hosts now. once all 6 have the rule we should see full recovery.
infra-bot: config-push completed: rule now active on all 6 hosts. health checks show 99.7% success on previously affected flows.
Sam: do we want to keep clamp long-term? what's root cause?
Anya: root cause hypothesis: upstream peer's firewall drops ICMPv6 PTB during heavy load and is configured to accept jumbo frames on their interface but not negotiate PMTU correctly. combined with our v6-preference we send large frames that never get MTU-reduced. Firmware update we pushed to our routers last night may also have changed offload handling (Jumbo enable).
Priya: log snippet from peer traceroute:```
traceroute6 to 2001:db8:service (via peer-asn 64521)
1 10ms 10ms 10ms
2 28ms 30ms 29ms !P PTB
3 * * *
```shows PTB but then nothing — suggests ICMPs filtered mid-path.
Sam: followups: 1) keep MSS clamp in place for az3-edge till upstream confirms fix or we change routing. 2) ask peer-asn to investigate ICMPv6 handling and jumbo settings. 3) schedule rollback test for last night's firmware to confirm correlation. 4) prepare postmortem.
Anya: I've opened ticket with upstream peer (case #UP-3221) and included pcap + header traces. asked them to validate ICMPv6 and jumbo negotiation.
Mike: I'm starting a controlled BGP canary now to shift 10% of traffic to IPv4 egress for the prefix to validate path stability. will monitor for regressions.```
Sam: monitor dashboards and customer signals for 30m. Priya please draft post-incident summary for later.
SupportOps: status page posted: "Intermittent connection errors for some IPv6 routes from az3; mitigation in place, impact reduced". link: https://status.redwood.example/incident/az3-1805
Anya: upstream replied — they confirmed ICMPv6 rate-limit caused PTB suppression during bursts. engineering will patch tomorrow morning. asked for rollback window if we need to change configs.
Mike: canary to IPv4 looks healthy so far (10%). no error increase. ready to expand if we need further mitigation.
Sam: good. handing off to Mike for next 6h monitoring window. I'll join postmortem. Mike you own timeline + customer comms.
Mike: taking oncall. will run hourly check-ins and escalate if anything spikes.
Sam: thanks team. add action items: investigate firmware change impact, long-term fix to prefer v4 for that peer or improve PMTUD resilience, and update runbooks for MSS clamp + BGP fallback.
SupportOps: customers notified of workaround. will coordinate follow-up comms once upstream confirms fix.
infra-bot: incident closed for immediate impact — mitigation stable. please file postmortem and tag eng-network and infra.
Sam: closing thread for now. tag me on the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
